title: Species-specific quantitative PCR (qPCR) protocol for Haplosporidium pinnae detection
author: Monserrat López-Sanmartín
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.xe7fjhn
materials: The qPCR assay for H. pinnae detection and quantification was carried out in duplicate using the species-specific primer pair (HpF3/HpR3) in a Mx3000P Thermocycler (Agilent).

steps.title: Prepare qPCR Reaction Mix
steps.instruction: Set up amplification reactions in a total volume of 10 µl.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 µl of PowerUpTM SYBRTM Green Master Mix (Applied Biosystems).
Include negative controls (without DNA or with H. pinnae non-infected fan mussel DNA, previously confirmed by qPCR).
Include positive controls (samples with positive cPCR amplification for H. pinnae).

steps.title: Run qPCR Thermal Cycling Program
steps.instruction: Execute the qPCR program using the following cycling conditions:

substeps.instruction: 40 cycles of: 95ºC for 15 s, 60ºC for 18 s, and 72ºC for 1 min
Perform a dissociation stage to determine the melt curve (Quantitative SYBR Green with dissociation curve)

steps.title: Generate Melting Curve
steps.instruction: Generate a melting curve to ensure a single PCR product was amplified.

steps.title: Calculate Standard Curves and Efficiency
steps.instruction: Calculate two standard curves and determine the efficiency (E).

substeps.instruction: Use serial dilutions of the plasmid and plasmid diluted with DNA of fan mussel for the curves.
Calculate efficiency (E) from the slope of the standard curve using the formula E=10-1/slope-1.

steps.title: Confirm Amplification via Electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Confirm the amplification results using agarose gel electrophoresis.

substeps.instruction: Run samples on 2% agarose gels in 1% TAE (Tris acetate EDTA buffer).
Stain gels with Red Safe (Nitron Biotechnology).
Scan using a GelDoc-It Imagen System Ultraviolet Transilluminator (BioImaging Systems).
